lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Who Eats Who?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about feeding relationships from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about what an animal eats.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about feeding relationships.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about what an animal eats at home.

lessons.title: Multiplication and Division Recap: 2, 5, 10
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall and apply 2, 5 and 10 times table facts.
success_criteria: I can recall 2, 5 and 10 times table facts.
I can solve a related division fact.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model recalling times table facts and their related division facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise recalling multiplication and matching division facts for 2, 5 and 10.
key_questions: What is the related division fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Recall 2, 5 and 10 times tables and related division facts fluently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record times table and inverse relationship understanding — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire times table and division quiz.
lessons.home_link: Practise the 2, 5 and 10 times tables together.

lessons.title: What Is a Food Chain?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a food chain shows.
success_criteria: I can say what a food chain shows.
I can use the word 'eaten by'.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap simple food chains from Year 1 (ocean).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce food chains formally, using arrows to show 'is eaten by'.
lessons.independent_task: Children order a simple food chain using picture cards and arrows.
key_questions: What comes first in this food chain?

differentiation.support: Order a 3-step food chain with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Order a 4+ step food chain independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note food chain sequencing understanding — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Think of a food chain with a family member.

lessons.title: Writing a Food Chain Sentence
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a sentence describing a food chain using 'is eaten by'.
success_criteria: I can write a food chain sentence.
I can use 'is eaten by' correctly.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap food chains ordered on Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a sentence describing a food chain using the correct structure.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 food chain sentences using 'is eaten by'.
key_questions: Can you write it as a sentence?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 3+ food chains as sentences independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of scientific vocabulary to sentence writing — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Describe a food chain to your family.

lessons.title: Solving Multiplication and Division Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve word problems involving multiplication and division.
success_criteria: I can solve a multiplication word problem.
I can solve a division word problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a food chain context (e.g. each bird eats 5 worms).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve multiplication and division word problems, showing working.

differentiation.greater_depth: Solve using facts for 2, 5 and 10 with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Record multiplication/division word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Make up a multiplication word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Where Does the Energy Come From?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain that food chains start with a plant.
success_criteria: I can say why food chains start with a plant.
I can identify the plant in a food chain.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss where plants get their energy (the sun).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why all food chains start with a plant, which gets energy from the sun.
lessons.independent_task: Children identify the starting plant in a range of food chains, explaining why it comes first.
key_questions: Why does this food chain start with a plant?
Where does the plant get its energy?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the energy source reasoning in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note deeper understanding of energy flow in food chains — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Recap why food chains start with plants.
lessons.home_link: Talk about where a plant's energy comes from.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Food Chain Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read food-chain-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read food chain words.
I can read a sentence about food chains.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to food-chain-themed words (e.g. 'plant', 'insect', 'energy').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading food chain words over the week.

lessons.title: Fractions Recap: Thirds, Quarters and Halves
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find thirds, quarters and halves of shapes and quantities confidently.
success_criteria: I can find a third, quarter and half of a shape.
I can find these fractions of a quantity.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all fractions learned so far this year.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate finding thirds, quarters and halves of shapes and quantities.
lessons.independent_task: Children find a range of fractions of given shapes and quantities.
key_questions: What is a third of this?
What is a quarter of this?

differentiation.support: Find halves and quarters with counters
differentiation.greater_depth: Find thirds, quarters and halves independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record fraction consolidation across three fraction types — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Find a third, quarter or half of a group of objects at home.

lessons.title: Building Our Own Food Chains
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a food chain using local habitat creatures.
success_criteria: I can build a food chain with 3+ links.
I can use arrows correctly.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap food chain examples seen this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model constructing a new food chain using local creatures studied (e.g. leaf, aphid, ladybird, bird).
lessons.independent_task: Children construct their own food chain using local creature picture cards.

differentiation.support: Construct a 3-link food chain with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Construct a 4+ link food chain independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of food chain construction skill using local examples — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Build a food chain with objects or drawings at home.

lessons.title: Explaining Our Food Chains
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain a food chain clearly to the class.
success_criteria: I can explain my food chain in order.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap food chains built on Wednesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear explanation of a food chain.
lessons.independent_task: Children explain their food chain to a small group, answering a question.

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and scientific explanation skill — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Explain your food chain to your family.

lessons.title: Position and Movement: Food Chain Diagrams
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use positional language to describe a food chain diagram.
success_criteria: I can describe what is first/last.
I can use positional language.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap positional language from earlier terms.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using positional language to describe the order of a food chain diagram.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe food chain diagrams using positional language, recording their descriptions.

differentiation.support: Use simple positional words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cross-curricular application of positional language — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Describe the order of something at home using positional words.

lessons.title: What Happens If a Link Is Removed?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to predict what might happen if part of a food chain disappears.
success_criteria: I can predict what might happen.
I can give a reason.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what might happen if one part of a food chain disappeared (e.g. no plants means no plant-eaters).
lessons.independent_task: Children predict and record what might happen if a link is removed from a chosen food chain.
key_questions: What would happen if this disappeared?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the knock-on effect through the whole chain

lessons.assessment_notes: Note deeper reasoning about interdependence in food chains — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Discuss what might happen if bees disappeared, with your family.

lessons.title: Food Chains Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about food chains.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's food chain learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about food chains, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What does a food chain show?
What might happen if a link disappeared?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on food chain facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Multiplication, Division, Fractions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply multiplication, division, and fraction skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can multiply and divide using 2, 5, 10 facts.
I can find thirds, quarters and halves.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of multiplication/division facts and fractions.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: multiplication/division, fractions.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 7 maths observations for each child, completing the Autumn 1 half-term — evidence for MATHS.N3/N4.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising times tables over the half-term break.

lessons.title: Food Chains Topic Recap and Autumn 1 Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about food chains, habitats and living things.
success_criteria: I can build and explain a food chain.
I can name a habitat and microhabitat.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole half-term's science learning (living things, habitats, microhabitats, food chains).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the half-term's learning about living things and their habitats.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a final class display celebrating the half-term's 'Living Things' learning.
key_questions: What have we learned about living things this half-term?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: End of half-term consolidation summary for the Living Things and Their Habitats unit — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a great first half-term of Year 2 science.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite science fact from this half-term with your family.
